text:
maya: FYI canary 2026-03-20 17:12 (model-infer:v2) is showing a latency tail increase in eu-west, 95p jumped from 120ms -> 420ms over the last 10m. Can we discuss rollback options?
oleg: ugh. seen the traces, looks KV miss storms on a hot prefix + session-affinity churn. error rate still low but p95s killing UX.
ravi: what are current traffic splits? I thought canary was at 8%?
maya: yes 8% global but ~22% of eu-west due to region weighting.
jen: quick question — do we prefer an immediate fast cut (flip canary to 0%) or a safe-drain (pause new canary traffic, let inflight finish, then evict cache)?
andre: prefer safe-drain unless it's catastrophic. fast cut is simple: update routing table -> 0, but we can leave stale KV state that might confuse roll-forward later.
maya: here's the telemetry trigger we used in console: p95 >= 300ms for 5m OR kv-miss-rate > 12% OR active-inflight-canary > 150 -> auto-guard. We hit p95 rule.
deploy-bot: [deploy event] canary-rollout model-infer:v2 -> 8% (eu-west weight 22%) by maya at 1905556700
oleg: plan I'm proposing: 1) immediate guard: set canary new-requests=0 (stop routing new sessions to canary), 2) mark canary-read-only for prefix sweep, 3) wait up to 90s for inflight to drain, 4) trigger kv-sweep job to reconcile keys with fallback, 5) set routing split to 0, 6) confirm metrics back to baseline.
ravi: small nit: step 2 (mark read-only) requires the canary runtime flag flip `--accept-new-sessions=false` + prevent sticky cookie issuance. Can we do both atomically?
jen: console UX: add a single action button "Pause new canary traffic and start KV reconcile" that runs both calls and shows expected completion timers. This would avoid manual curl juggling during incidents.
andre: agree but we need an escape hatch to fast-cut if drain isn't reducing p95 quickly. propose a 2-min watchdog after pause -> if p95 still > 300ms then set split=0 immediately.
maya: sounds good. what's the curl sequence if we have to do manual? putting into thread: 
```
# pause new canary sessions
curl -X POST https://internal.redwood/api/rollouts/controls \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"id":"canary-2026-03-20","accept_new":false}'

# kick kv reconcile (namespace: session-prefix-xyz)
curl -X POST https://internal.redwood/api/kv/reconcile \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"namespace":"session-prefix-xyz","mode":"two-way-sweep"}'

# if needed, set traffic split to 0
curl -X POST https://internal.redwood/api/rollouts/split \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"canary_percent":0}'
```
oleg: for kv reconcile we should also set a short TTL on canary-inserted keys so they don't survive long if we flip. `SET key ttl 60` style via batch job. Otherwise reintroducing canary later will have inconsistent state.
ravi: agree. add a reconcile verification step: sample 200 keys, assert fallback-values match canary-values after sweep, and fail if mismatch > 2%.
jen: telemetry additions: surface an estimated time-to-drain in console using current inflight count / avg request duration so operator knows whether to wait or fast-cut. Put a prominent red CTA for fast-cut.
andre: also important: if customer quotas are in play, flipping traffic might move requests to a different quota bucket and cause rate-limits. Ensure quota-exempt fallback or pre-warm quotas.
maya: good catch — we did see a secondary 429 spike in staging once when we flipped without pre-warming. add pre-warm step: call quota-service with expected qps bump.
sre-bot: incident checkpoint: created incident INC-2026-2048 for canary p95 spike, assigned to eng-platform oncall.
oleg: ok executing: pausing new canary sessions now.
maya: thanks. initiating kv-sweep job, TTL policy applied to canary keys = 60s.
ravi: inflight count at pause = 138, avg duration 420ms, est drain time ~ (138 * 0.42) / concurrency factor ~ 15-30s depending on concurrency.
jen: watching metrics. if after 90s p95 still > 300 then i'll press fast-cut.
deploy-bot: [action complete] canary accept_new=false set by oleg at 1905557002
deploy-bot: [job start] kv-reconcile job started for session-prefix-xyz at 1905557005
maya: kv reconcile reports 0.8% mismatch after sample check, within threshold.
andre: good. inflight now 12.
ravi: can we hold 30s and then set split=0?
jen: waiting 30s...
jen: pressing fast-cut now (split -> 0).
deploy-bot: [rollout update] canary-2026-03-20 split set to 0 by jen at 1905557130
maya: monitoring... p95 dropping back to ~110ms in eu-west. no 4xx spikes. looks healthy.
oleg: follow-up items: - add console combined action (pause+kv-reconcile+pre-warm) - add telemetry field for est-draintime - ensure quota pre-warm contract in routing docs - add postmortem prompt in incident flow to capture whether fast-cut was used and why.
jen: filing follow-up ticket ENG-ops-472 for console action + telemetry.
maya: thanks everyone. marking thread resolved when postmortem ticket has been created.
andre: :thumbsup:
